title: A RISC-V Vector Extension for Multi-word Arithmetic
problem: Multi-word arithmetic (operands exceeding native word size) is critical for HPC; carry-propagation bottlenecks limit performance; GPU approaches less energy-efficient; DSA designs incur high non-recurring engineering costs
motivation: Explore RISC-V potential for HPC through custom architectural extensions supporting multi-word arithmetic more efficiently than GPUs or specialized accelerators
method: Model-based RISC-V Vector (RVV) extension for multi-word operations; comprehensive performance modeling across diverse microarchitectures; evaluation on number theoretic transform and post-quantum cryptography kernels
key_novelty: General modeling-based multi-word arithmetic extension on RISC-V; carry-propagation enhancement through architectural extension
contributions: General modeling-based multi-word extension on RISC-V Vector ISA
Comprehensive performance models for diverse microarchitectures
Validation on cryptographic kernels (NTT, post-quantum crypto)
limitations: Abstract lacks specific performance improvements over baselines; energy efficiency metrics not provided; practical deployment considerations not discussed
